title: Transfer: gravity and motion
target: Apply gravity, projectile and orbital reasoning to a new set of cases.
criteria: State a model and assumptions before calculating.
Connect diagrams to forces and motion.
Check units and explain the limits of conclusions.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Which statement defines an ideal horizontal-launch model before calculation?
options: Horizontal speed increases because gravity points forward.
Initial vertical velocity is zero, air resistance is negligible, and g is uniform.
cpa.guide: These assumptions justify independent constant-horizontal and accelerated-vertical motion.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A horizontal launch falls 5 m with g = 10 m/s² and no drag. What is fall time?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A car turns at constant speed. Which net-force direction matches its curved motion?
cpa.guide: Turning velocity requires inward acceleration and net force.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A probe’s center distance from a planet doubles. Its field was 16 N/kg. What are the new field and force on a 3 kg mass?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A projectile range calculation yields a value in m/s. What should be checked?
options: The equations and units, because range must be a length.
Only whether the mass is positive.
cpa.guide: Dimensional consistency is a necessary check.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: An asteroid’s ideal path crosses Earth’s orbit. What conclusion is justified from that fact alone?
options: A collision is not established without matching timing and spatial geometry.
cpa.guide: Path intersection alone omits simultaneous positions and uncertainty.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
